introduction:
Property registration in Rajasthan is a mandatory process governed by the Registration Act, 1908. Registering your property secures legal ownership, establishes your title, and protects against future ownership disputes.

The process is managed online via the e-Panjiyan system (epanjiyan.rajasthan.gov.in). While initial application and payments are completed online, a physical visit to the local Sub-Registrar's Office (SRO) is mandatory for biometric verification.
quickFacts:
Quick Facts & Key Details
  • Method: Online application (mandatory to generate tracking ID) + Physical Visit to SRO.
  • Processing Time: Same day (if documents are correct and slot is booked).
  • Stamp Duty (2026 Estimates): ~6% of property value for Men, ~5% for Women.
  • Labor Cess: 20% surcharge on the Stamp Duty amount (not property value).
  • Registration Fee: 1% of the property value (for all applicants).
  • Total Cost: Approx. 8.2% (Men) to 7% (Women) of the property value.
  • Portal: e-Panjiyan Portal (epanjiyan.rajasthan.gov.in).
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: Prepare all original documents and one set of clear photocopies before starting your application.
Property & Value Proofs
  • Ownership Proof: Original Sale Deed, Title Deed, or Allotment Letter.
  • Property Details: Property Chain documents (past owners) and Map/Plan of the property.
  • Value Proof: DLC Rate (District Level Committee rate) or Valuation Report.
  • NOC: No Objection Certificate (if applicable, e.g., from Housing Society).
Personal ID & Witnesses
  • Identity Proof: Aadhaar Card and PAN Card of both Buyer and Seller.
  • Photographs: Two passport-size photos each of the Buyer and Seller.
  • Witnesses: Two witnesses with their valid ID proofs (Aadhaar/Voter ID).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Step-by-Step Online Application & Valuation

Every applicant must generate a "Citizen Reference Number" (CRN) online. Follow this flow to submit your details:

Step 1: Registration on e-Panjiyan
  • Go to the e-Panjiyan portal.
  • Click on "Online Property Valuation & Registration".
  • Create a "New User" account or log in if you have existing credentials.
Step 2: Property Valuation
  • Select your District, Tehsil, and Village/Colony.
  • Enter exact property details (Area in sq ft/meters, residential/commercial type).
  • The system will automatically calculate the Stamp Duty and Registration Fees based on current DLC rates.
Step 3: Document Upload & Data Entry
  • Enter details of the Party (Buyer/Seller names, PAN, Aadhaar) and Witnesses.
  • Upload scanned copies of ID proofs and the draft Deed (Draft Sale Deed).
  • Click Save to generate your Citizen Reference Number (CRN). Keep this number safe.
Step 4: Payment (e-GRAS)
  • The portal will redirect you to the e-GRAS system for payment.
  • Pay the Stamp Duty and Registration Fee via Net Banking or Credit Card.
  • Print the e-Challan receipt as your proof of payment.
Step 5: Slot Booking
  • After completing the payment, return to the e-Panjiyan portal.
  • Select and book a convenient Time Slot for your physical visit to the Sub-Registrar (SR) Office.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Assisted Application Services (Offline Help)

Purely offline handwritten applications are not accepted without a digital CRN. If you cannot use a computer, use these assisted services:

  1. Visit an e-Mitra Kiosk: Go to any authorized e-Mitra center in Rajasthan. The operator will fill out the online form, scan your documents, pay the fees, and generate your CRN for a nominal service fee.
  2. Hire a Deed Writer/Advocate: Visit the court or SR office complex. Licensed Deed Writers can draft your sale deed, complete the online data entry, make payments, and hand over the file ready for signature.
  3. Mandatory Physical Submission: Regardless of who fills out the forms, both the Buyer and Seller must physically visit the Sub-Registrar's office for the final signature and biometrics.
afterApplying:
Physical SRO Visit & Mutation (Next Steps)

At the Sub-Registrar (SR) Office:
  • Reporting: Report to the SR office 15 minutes before your slot with the CRN, Original Documents, e-Challan, and witnesses.
  • Verification & Biometrics: The SR verifies the uploaded details. Buyer, Seller, and witnesses provide fingerprints and digital photos via webcam.
  • Endorsement & Delivery: The Sub-Registrar signs and endorses the deed. The registered Sale Deed (Registry) is returned immediately or within 24 hours.
CRITICAL NEXT STEP: Mutation (Naam Namantran)

Property registration is not final proof of ownership for tax purposes. You must update revenue records:

  1. Submit the registered deed to the local Patwari (rural) or Municipal Corporation/UIT (urban).
  2. Apply for Mutation (name change in Jamabandi), which can also be done online via e-Mitra.
  3. This ensures property taxes and utility bills (e.g., electricity) are issued in your name.
